meta.titulo: Where Is Digital Sovereignty at Stake?
meta.descripcion: Master's thesis in Applied Ethics (UC) by Alejandro Bustos Núñez on the technical condition of authority and legitimacy in digital sovereignty, and the projects built around it.

titulo: Where Is Digital Sovereignty at Stake? Analyzing the Technical Condition of Authority and Legitimacy for Democratic States

lineas: To Mom and Dad, here and in heaven
To the public education that formed me
For Ana, for her inspiration even from afar
And to Raúl, for the conversations and a profound acceptance

resumen: The literature on digital sovereignty assesses legitimacy at the ends of the relationship between the State and technology: in the procedure that authorizes a norm and in the outcomes it produces. This article argues that the legitimacy of digital sovereignty also depends on a technical condition, and that procedural assessment is therefore insufficient in principle. Ethics requires that a system retain the capacity to transform its own norms, and so it must co-individuate with the system. Digital systems, however, operate recursively, absorbing external norms as parameters they optimize on their own terms. The article calls this phenomenon recursive capture. A technical norm that operates as a social norm and that those affected cannot transform amounts to domination, even when it comes from a democratic procedure. From this follows a criterion that distinguishes legitimate authority over a technical system from jurisdiction over its territory.

proyectos.titulo: What is being built around it
proyectos.intro: The thesis is not the center of these projects: it is one more node in an anisomorphic network, where each piece has its own form and connects to the others for different reasons. While writing it I kept starting other projects, some in direct consonance with it and others more peripheral, that ask the same question from the community and from practice: what does it mean to keep the capacity to transform the norms of the systems that govern us?

cooperativa.bajada: A cooperative whose members host their own infrastructure and receive a Solid pod with an open identity (WebID). It is the inverse of Cerrillos: the community anticipates its own associated milieu.

software.bajada: espacio and a set of small apps that separate data from the application, so anyone can replace or abandon an app without losing what is theirs.

arquitecturas.bajada: Architecture notes on Solid and Linked Data: another way of coupling system and milieu, with infrastructure distributed across homes instead of hyperscale data centers.

estetica.bajada: An ethics that emerges in individuation, instead of applying norms to given objects. I cut it from the thesis text for length.

audioteca.bajada: Narrated audio with open voices: a podcast on Simondon's Individuation and another that unfolds the thesis argument.

cuentos.bajada: Sael: speculative fiction about a digital technician in a society organized in mesh networks after a crisis.

red.aria: Network of interconnected projects; the thesis is one of the nodes

criterios.intro: Three conditions I propose in the thesis to judge whether a democratic State, or a community, exercises legitimate authority over a technical system or only jurisdiction over its territory. The criterion is gradual: it admits degrees of authority. Pick a case, move the values and compare the shapes. Cerrillos is the thesis case; the others are hypothetical and small-scale.

ui.radar: Radar chart of the three conditions of legitimate authority
ui.nota: The values are my own reading, meant for thinking with. They are not a measurement.

ejes.pregunta: Does the relationship preserve the capacity to transform the system's norms, beyond its recursive adaptation?
Does the institution take part as interpreter and coordinator of the relationship, and not only as a source of norms when authorizing or sanctioning?
Does that participation remain open to citizen contestation, in terms of non-domination?

cerrillos.resumen: The system absorbed the court's requirement as a design parameter: Google switched to air cooling and the project left the scope of the assessment. The State only authorized and sanctioned. One resident's legal challenge was the only channel of contestation. The result: jurisdiction without authority.

mesh.resumen: A neighborhood builds and maintains its own antenna network with open firmware. Neighbors understand the system because they set it up, change it when the milieu changes and can disconnect it without the neighborhood collapsing.

liceo.nombre: High school with a proprietary school platform
liceo.resumen: A school contracts a cloud platform with no access to the code or to exportable data. The vendor defines the design, the school only readjusts, and leaving the platform would cost a year of teachers' work.

municipio.nombre: Municipality with a free-software permit desk
municipio.resumen: A town's IT team migrates its permit desk to free software and runs open workshops to read the code. It gains the ability to read and to change the system, but residents do not yet take part in design decisions.

agua.nombre: Rural water committee with open sensors
agua.resumen: A rural drinking-water committee installs open-design moisture sensors and keeps the data in its own pod. Neighbors took part from the first prototype, though the committee depends on a single technician.

consultorio.nombre: Clinic with a single-vendor medical record
consultorio.resumen: A clinic uses a medical record system whose format cannot be exported. Staff can operate it but not read it, and changing vendors would mean retyping years of patient histories.

pie.traduccion: The English and Russian versions are my draft translations.

abordar.intro: There is no single door. Depending on where you come from, this thesis can be read, listened to or explored. Pick an entry point.

caso.bajada: A data center, an aquifer under water stress and a resident who took the project to court: the case that opens the thesis. A short note points you to the audio library and the three conditions.

simondon.bajada: The thesis rests on his critique of the hylomorphic scheme and his distinction between norms and values, which Yuk Hui extends to the recursivity of digital systems. I am preparing a podcast on Individuation so you can enter it without being a philosopher.

audio.bajada: A podcast with a four-chapter script that unfolds the argument on digital sovereignty.

texto.bajada: An article of about 5,200 words, under review until November 30, 2026. For now the file is a test.
